full_judgment:
3. The case of the plaintiff, in short, was that Mirzakhil Darbar Sharif was founded by Hazrat Moulana Shah Sufi Moqlesur Rahman, grandfather of Hazrat Moulana Moksurur Rahman. After his death, his son Hazrat Moulana Abdul Hye became the second Sazzadanashin and thereafter Hazrat Moulana Moqlesur Rahman became the third Sazzadanshin of the said Darbar Sharif. They were great Saints. They have disciples within and outside the country and every year three urs, jikir-askar, jiarat and other religious functions were held and large congregations of muridans and devotees arrived at Darbar Sharif and during urs and the other religious festivals, many disciples and muridans stayed at the guest house built in the suit land and the other lands around Darbar Sharif. Due to the pre-occupation of the Sazzadanashin, the properties of Darbar Sharif are usually managed and administered by Khadems and Attorneys on behalf of Darbar Sharif under the instruction of the Sazzadanashin. During the time when Moulana Moqlesur Rahman became the third Sazzadanashin, he caused the suit property to be purchased for Darbar Sharif with it's funds in benami of one of its most trusted and old Khadem Mahan Miah Chowdhury. Since the date of purchase and by erection of house on the suit property by Darbar Sharif as a guest house for the accommodation of disciples coming from distant places during Urs and other religious festivals, it was being used for such purpose. The P.S. and the B.S. Khatians were prepared in the name of benamdar, Madan Miah Chowdhury and the rents were paid by Darbar Sharif in the name of the benamdar and even those khatians show that the guest houses are used by the devotes and the disciples as the guests during their stay at the time of religious festival. The suit property in reality never belonged to or was owned by Khadem Madan Miah Chowdhury. The residence of Madan Miah Chowdhury was about 4/5 miles away from the suit mouza in Rupkani, the suit property was all along in possession of Darbar Sharif since the date of its purchase. During the life time of Madan Miah Chaowdhury, he never claimed the suit property as his own. At the relevant time, the other properties were also acquired by Darbar Sharif in benami of Khadem Madan Miah Chowdhury, defendant Nos. 2 to 5 by executing a nadabi deed dated 24.10.1994, i.e. during the pendency of the instant suit. The document of title of the suit property, namely, patta of 1943 was kept in the custody of Darbar Sharif. Khadem Madan Miah Chowdhury was given the said patta sometimes in 1966 in order to enable him to defend Miscellaneous Appeal No. 122 of 1966 brought by Motalebur Rahman, a step brother of Hazrat Moulana Moqlesur Rahman. Khadem Madan Miah Chowdhury filed the said patta in the aforesaid case by firisty on 07.04.1966 and thereafter, the said patta was taken back by him from the Court. The patta was thereafter required to be used for paying rents of the suit property and as result, the same was retained by him. But before the said patta was returned to the Sazzadanshin of Darbar Sharif; Khadem Madan Miah Chowdhury died in 1985. Accordingly, the original of the patta remained with the heirs of Hkadem Madan Miah Chowdhury, i.e. defendant Nos. 2 to 5. Subsequently actuated by ill motive, defendant Nos. 2 to 5 executed and registered the sale deed in question on 13.07.1992 in favour of defendant No.1 purporting to sell the suit property to him. Hence, the plaintiff was constrained to file the present suit for the aforementioned relief. 

 10. From the judgment of the Courts below, it appears that both the Courts considering the evidence, oral and documentary, in detail gave clear finding that the plaintiff failed to prove the ingredients of benami transaction, such as, possession of the suit property, the source of money in purchasing the suit property, the custody of the patta by which the suit property was purchased by Modan Miah Chowdhury and the motive behind the benami purchase as claimed by the plaintiff. In coming to the said finding, the Courts below gave specific finding on each of the said ingredients. The Courts below held that the plaintiff failed to substantiate his case that the suit property was purchased in the benami of Madan Miah Chowdhury due to the enmity with his step brothers and that there were other properties purchased in the name of the Sazzadanashin and Darbar Sharif and that there was no reason to purchase the suit property in the name of Madan Miah Chowdhury, a rich man; Madan Miah Chowdhury himself paid the consideration money for the purchase of the suit property and the plaintiff failed to prove that the money was paid by Darbar Sharif; the original patta was produced from the custody of defendant No.1 who purchased the suit property from the heirs of Madan Miah Chwodhury (defendant Nos. 2-5) and that the plaintiff failed to substantiate the story as to the production of the original patta from the custody of defendant No.1; Madan Miah Chowdhury had been in possession of the suit property since purchase by patta dated 18.11.1943 and after his death, it was defendant Nos. 2-5 who were in possession thereof and after purchase, it is defendant No.1 who is in possession thereof; the plaintiff failed to prove that the muridans and the devotees of Darbar Sharif used to live a the house erected on the land in dispute as the property of Darbar Sharif and that the two records of rights, namely, the P.S. Khatian and the B.S. Khatian were prepared in the name of the defendants and that the rents were paid by Madan Miah Chowdhury and since 1934 till the filing of the suit at no point of time, Darbar Sharif claimed the suit property as its own.
